We will use the fact that the dot product is linear.

To quickly compute the numerator $(5u)\cdot v,$ we multiply $u\cdot v$ by $5.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(5u)\cdot v & =5(u\cdot v) \\  & =5\cdot (-1) \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

To quickly compute the denominator $v\cdot (\frac{1}{2}v),$ we compute $v\cdot v$ first and then multiply the result by $\frac{1}{2}.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot (\frac{1}{2}v) & =\frac{1}{2}(v\cdot v) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}+{v}_{5}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{5}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+4+4+0+25) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 34 \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{(5u)\cdot v}{v\cdot (\frac{1}{2}v)}=-\frac{5}{17}.
$$
